newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HOWARD OUTLINES PLANS FOR ECONOMIC GROWTH
Prime Minister John Howard's told the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry keeping inflation, wages growth and interest rates under control are the keys to long term economic growth.
Speaking at the chamber's annual dinner, Mr Howard said other important aims include steady microeconomic reform, the lowering of protectionism and the development of a strong competition policy.
Mr Howard said if all these aims can be met by his Government, it should be able to deliver sustainable economic growth and lower unemployment.
His underscoring of the importance of competition policy and the lowering of protectionist trade barriers here and abroad comes after concern expressed by some National Party members.
KEATING: HOWARD SLOW ON RACE DEBATE
Former Prime Minister, Paul Keating, says it's up to the Federal Government to ensure Australia's good reputation for racial tolerance isn't sullied by the current race debate.
Speaking at the University of New South Wales in his second lecture as visiting Professor, Mr Keating criticised his successor as Prime Minister, John Howard, for not settling the debate earlier.
Mr Keating said politicians must understand the confusion facing many Australians if they're to deal effectively with the present racism debate, prompted by Independent Federal M-P, Pauline Hanson.
He says if Australia's good name for tolerance and fair play is damaged, the fault will lie with the Government, not the Australian people or Ms Hanson.
BRITISH WIN RAAF TRAINING AIRCRAFT CONTRACT
The Federal Government has chosen British Aerospace as the potential supplier of training aircraft for the RAAF for the next 25 years.
Defence Minister, Ian McLachlan, says the new Hawk jets will provide a modern digital cockpit trainer and replace the RAAF's ageing Macchi trainer aircraft fleet.
Mr McLachlan says British Aerospace has offered an advanced version of its successful Hawk trainer aircraft which is used by the airforces of the United Kingdom, Switzerland and regional countries.
Australian industry will be involved in the assembly, testing and on-going support of the new aircraft, with the main support facility located at Newcastle airport in New South Wales.
BRITISH PENSION POLICY COSTS AUSSIES
Federal Social Security Minister, Jocelyn Newman, says British pensioners who migrate to Australia are forced to hold out a begging bowl to the Government to avoid sliding into poverty.
Senator Newman says Britain's refusal to accept reciprocal pension rights between the two countries costs the Federal Government about 80 million dollars a year.
Speaking in London after a meeting with her counterpart, Peter Lilley, Senator Newman said the position was immoral and indefensible.
Senator Newman says she offered a compromise deal to Mr Lilley, but it was rejected.
FOSTER TO BE SENTENCED TODAY
A District Court Judge is today pondering the fate of 34-year-old Gold Coast conman, Peter Foster.
Final submissions have been made in the case, and the judge must now decide what sentence to impose on the defendant.
Peter Foster pleaded guilty to three counts of corrupting three people who consequently gave false evidence to an Australian Security Commission inquiry into a company called Tradex.
It's alleged the defendant was managing the company while still an undischarged bankrupt.
He's also admitted to using a false passport to gain entry to Australia last month.
Judge Newton will hand down his decision on Friday morning.
ACCI PRESIDENT SLAMS LIVING WAGE CLAIM
The President of the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry has described the ACTU's Living Wage claim as a cruel hoax, and an across the board wage rise in disguise.
Graeme Samuel says that if successful, the claim would stall economic growth, slash investment, and cause unemployment to skyrocket.
Prime Minister, John Howard says there are legitimate concerns about the claim ..although he believes working men and women deserve gratitude for wage restraint.
Mr Samuel says that what award wage earners would gain in a wage rise, they would lose through higher interest rates, higher inflation and fewer jobs.
MALAYSIA OPPOSITION DISAPPOINTED WITH AUSTRALIA
Malaysia's Deputy Opposition leader says he's very disappointed with the Australian Government's response to the event in Kuala Lumpur at the weekend.
Lim Guan Eng says the Australian Government should have shown more backbone and defended its citizens.
He was commenting on the detention of a number of Australians, including ABC jounalist Catherine McGrath, among activists attending a conference on East Timor.
Mr Lim, the deputy leader of the Opposition Democractic Action Party, says Australian citizens deserve more support from their governemnt.
QUAYLE RESIGNATION "A BLOW TO RUGBY LEAGUE"
Parramatta chief executive Dennis Fitzgerald says the resignation of General Manager John Quayle is a blow to the Australian Rugby League as it prepares to meet SuperLeague head-on next season.
John Quayle has resigned his position as ARL general manager but his official reasons won't be known until tomorrow.
Mr Fitzgerald believes Mr Quayle's departure does not herald any deal between the ARL and Superleague.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
